knowledge_point.title: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{1} x e^{2 x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $I$ denote the given integral. Choose the factors so that differentiating the linear factor simplifies the remaining integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}
u&=x, & u^\prime&=1,\\
v^\prime&=e^{2 x}, & v&=\frac{e^{2 x}}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the definite integration-by-parts formula:

$$
\int_a^b uv^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x=[uv]_a^b-\int_a^b vu^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[\frac{x e^{2 x}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}\\
&\quad-\int_{0}^{1}\left(\frac{e^{2 x}}{2}\right)\left(1\right)\,\mathrm{d}x,\\
&=\left[\frac{x e^{2 x}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}-\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}e^{2 x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate the remaining function and combine the two primitive terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[\frac{x e^{2 x}}{2} - \frac{e^{2 x}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $F(x)$ denote the primitive inside the brackets. Evaluate each endpoint, then subtract the entire lower value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F\left(1\right)&=\frac{e^{2}}{4}=\frac{e^{2}}{4},\\
F\left(0\right)&=- \frac{1}{4}=- \frac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left(\frac{e^{2}}{4}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{4} + \frac{e^{2}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}} - x e^{- 3 x}\,\mathrm{d}x=
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $I$ denote the given integral. Choose the factors so that differentiating the linear factor simplifies the remaining integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}
u&=- x, & u^\prime&=-1,\\
v^\prime&=e^{- 3 x}, & v&=- \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the definite integration-by-parts formula:

$$
\int_a^b uv^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x=[uv]_a^b-\int_a^b vu^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[\frac{x e^{- 3 x}}{3}\right]_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}\\
&\quad-\int_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}\left(- \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{3}\right)\left(-1\right)\,\mathrm{d}x,\\
&=\left[\frac{x e^{- 3 x}}{3}\right]_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}-\frac{1}{3}\int_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}e^{- 3 x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate the remaining function and combine the two primitive terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[\frac{x e^{- 3 x}}{3} + \frac{e^{- 3 x}}{9}\right]_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $F(x)$ denote the primitive inside the brackets. Evaluate each endpoint, then subtract the entire lower value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)&=\frac{2}{9 e}=\frac{2}{9 e},\\
F\left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)&=- \frac{e^{2}}{9}=- \frac{e^{2}}{9}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left(\frac{2}{9 e}\right)-\left(- \frac{e^{2}}{9}\right)\\
&=\frac{2 + e^{3}}{9 e}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{1} - 2 x e^{- 2 x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $I$ denote the given integral. Choose the factors so that differentiating the linear factor simplifies the remaining integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}
u&=- 2 x, & u^\prime&=-2,\\
v^\prime&=e^{- 2 x}, & v&=- \frac{e^{- 2 x}}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the definite integration-by-parts formula:

$$
\int_a^b uv^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x=[uv]_a^b-\int_a^b vu^\prime\,\mathrm{d}x.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[x e^{- 2 x}\right]_{0}^{1}\\
&\quad-\int_{0}^{1}\left(- \frac{e^{- 2 x}}{2}\right)\left(-2\right)\,\mathrm{d}x,\\
&=\left[x e^{- 2 x}\right]_{0}^{1}-\int_{0}^{1}e^{- 2 x}\,\mathrm{d}x.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate the remaining function and combine the two primitive terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left[x e^{- 2 x} + \frac{e^{- 2 x}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $F(x)$ denote the primitive inside the brackets. Evaluate each endpoint, then subtract the entire lower value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F\left(1\right)&=\frac{3}{2 e^{2}}=\frac{3}{2 e^{2}},\\
F\left(0\right)&=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=\left(\frac{3}{2 e^{2}}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{3 - e^{2}}{2 e^{2}}.
\end{aligned}
$$
